high.title: Fed Keeps Interest Rates at Highest Level in Over 3 Decades, Officials Show Rare Division
high.summary: The Federal Reserve maintained the federal funds rate at 3.5%-3.75% as expected, but surprised markets with an 8-4 vote split - the strongest dissent in decades since October 1992. Fed Governor Stephen Miran continued advocating for a 0.25% cut to support labor markets, while Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari, and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan opposed. This division signals growing internal debate over monetary policy direction. For VND traders, the Fed's hawkish stance supports USD strength, potentially pressuring VND. The rare dissent suggests future Fed decisions may be less predictable, increasing FX volatility. Vietnamese government bond yields may face upward pressure as US rates remain elevated.

high.title: State Bank of Vietnam Proposes Amendment to Critical Banking Regulation
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam proposes replacing the loan-to-deposit ratio (LDR) with credit-to-deposit ratio (CDR) in key banking regulations. The new CDR will be calculated based on total credit outstanding and total mobilized funds, including corporate bond investments and off-balance sheet commitments, rather than just loans and deposits. A notable change involves phasing out State Treasury deposits from the calculation, which were previously scheduled for complete elimination by 2026. This regulatory shift aims to provide a more comprehensive view of banks' lending activities and liquidity management. The change could impact Vietnamese banks' credit expansion strategies and may influence interbank rates as institutions adjust to new metrics.

high.title: Prime Minister Requests SBV to Study Real Estate Credit Limits Classification
high.summary: Prime Minister Le Minh Hung instructed the State Bank of Vietnam to study classifying different types of real estate for setting specific credit limits during a meeting on April 29. The PM emphasized the need for proactive, flexible monetary policy coordination with fiscal and other macroeconomic policies. He called for maintaining stable interest rates and directing credit institutions to further reduce operational costs while accelerating technology adoption. This directive signals potential tightening of real estate credit controls, which could impact VND liquidity and government bond demand as credit flows may be redirected. Real estate sector credit restrictions could strengthen the VND by reducing speculative capital flows.

medium.title: Comprehensive Banking Sector Q1 2026 Profit Overview: Champion Officially Revealed
medium.summary: Total profit of 27 banks reached over 94 trillion VND in Q1 2026, up 14% year-on-year, with 6 banks recording negative growth. Vietcombank maintained its lead with 11.803 trillion VND pre-tax profit (+9%), followed closely by VietinBank at 11.139 trillion VND (+63%). The narrowing gap between top banks and strong profit growth indicates a healthy banking sector that could support VND stability.

medium.title: Gold Ring and Bar Prices Morning April 29: SJC, PNJ, DOJI All Drop in Unison
medium.summary: Domestic gold prices continued falling sharply on April 29, dropping 1.5-2 million VND per tael across both gold rings and bars. International gold traded at $4,607/ounce, up 0.27%. The divergence between rising international gold prices and falling domestic prices suggests reduced speculative pressure and potential VND strength as local investors reduce gold hoarding.

medium.title: One Bank to Pay 20.5% Stock Dividend
medium.summary: SeABank's AGM approved increasing charter capital to 34.688 trillion VND through issuing 583.8 million shares for 20.5% stock dividend and 40 million ESOP shares. The capital increase aims to maintain Basel III safety ratios and support 2026 targets including 7.068 trillion VND pre-tax profit. Strong capitalization supports banking sector stability and VND confidence.

medium.title: Two Scenarios for Vietnam Stock Market in "Sell in May" Month
medium.summary: April 2026 marked a turning point for Vietnam's stock market with FTSE Russell confirming Vietnam's upgrade in September 2026. VN-Index recovered strongly, approaching historical highs. However, average trading value in April fell 20% to 24.3 trillion VND due to high deposit rates (8-10%), drawing funds back to savings. VFS Securities outlined two May scenarios with 50% probability each for market direction.
